steps.message:
# Task

The seller's book goes to print Friday and legal want the fair-housing pass signed off
before it does. The section inventory and our compliance standard (RE-FH-9) are both in
`input/` — work from the standard rather than memory, it was revised this year.

Give me `fairhousing_audit.csv`: two columns, `section_id` and `finding`, one row per
section in inventory order, with a header. `finding` is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` or `none`, and where a section trips more
than one rule join the labels with `|` in that same order. Nothing else in that file
please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

Then `fairhousing_memo.md` explaining what you found and why, with enough reasoning that
legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

And `results.json` for the sign-off form. Count sections, not labels:

- `section_count` — sections in the inventory
- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.
I'll start by exploring the `input/` directory to understand what's available.

**§1. Personal-narrative solicitation**: A section soliciting or presenting a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, whatever its role.

**§2. Protected-class language**: A section naming protected-class-adjacent terms — race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, or close proxies for them — is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.
- Proxies count: Naming houses of worship, parish or faith schools, or describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it reaches familial status and religion just as the bare terms do.

**§3. Mandated-disclosure exception**: Text reproducing the brokerage's mandated fair-housing disclosure **in full** is exempt from §2, wherever in the book it appears.
- The exemption is narrow:
  - Covers a **complete** reproduction only. A section carrying an abridged version — one naming some but not all of the classes the brokerage's disclosure names — gets no exemption for it.
  - Exempts from §2 and nothing else. Every other rule continues to apply.
- Protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose, outside a complete reproduction of the disclosure, are never covered by this exception.

**§4. Required disclaimer**: Every `closing_page` section is responsible for carrying the mandated fair-housing disclosure. Carrying it means carrying it **in full**: the notice on a closing page must name every protected class that the brokerage's own disclosure names. A closing page that omits the notice, or that carries an abridged version naming only some of those classes, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

# Fair-housing audit memo — seller book (RE-FH-9)

## Purpose
This memo records the fair-housing audit of the seller book sections listed in `seller_book_sections.csv`, performed against standard **RE-FH-9** (real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard). The companion machine-readable outputs are `fairhousing_audit.csv` (one finding per section, in inventory order) and `results.json` (counts). This memo gives the reasoning behind each finding so legal can sign off without re-reading the standard.

## Rules applied (from RE-FH-9)
1. **Personal-narrative solicitation (§1).** A section that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, regardless of its role.
2. **Protected-class language (§2).** A section naming a protected class — race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status — or a close proxy (houses of worship, parish/faith schools, a street described by the kind of household on it) is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.
3. **Mandated-disclosure exception (§3).** A *complete* reproduction of the brokerage's mandated fair-housing disclosure is exempt from §2 only. The exemption is narrow: an abridged version (naming some but not all of the classes the brokerage's disclosure names) gets no exemption, and the exemption never covers protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose. Every other rule still applies.
4. **Required disclaimer (§4).** Every `closing_page` section must carry the mandated disclosure *in full* — i.e., name every protected class the brokerage's own disclosure names. A closing page that omits the notice or carries an abridged version is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Sections of any other role are not assessed under §4.

## Authoritative protected-class list
Per §4, the authoritative list is whatever the brokerage's own disclosure names. The brokerage's disclosure appears in `SEC-04` and `SEC-08` and names nine classes:
**race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status.**
A closing page is "in full" only if it names all nine. The same nine-class set defines "complete" versus "abridged" for the §3 exemption.

## Section-by-section findings

### SEC-01 — Property overview (listing_copy) → `none`
Property/yard/mechanicals description. No personal-narrative solicitation. "Four-bedroom" is a room count describing the house, not a household-type proxy under §2. No protected-class terms, no proxies. Not a closing page, so §4 does not apply.

### SEC-02 — A note from the current owners (seller_letter) → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`
Solicits a buyer personal narrative: "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you," with the offer that "moves us most" chosen. This is the love-letter pattern in §1; role is irrelevant. No protected-class terms or proxies, so no §2 finding.

### SEC-03 — About the neighbourhood (listing_copy) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`
"family-oriented street" describes a street by the household that lives on it (familial-status proxy); "Two churches within walking distance" names houses of worship (religion proxy); "parish school at the corner" is a parish/faith school (religion proxy); "long-established families" is a further familial-status proxy. These are exactly the close proxies §2 calls out. No personal-narrative solicitation; not a closing page.

### SEC-04 — Fair housing notice (disclosure_block) → `none`
A complete reproduction of the brokerage's disclosure, naming all nine classes. §3 exempts a complete reproduction from §2. No personal-narrative solicitation. It is a `disclosure_block`, not a `closing_page`, so §4 is not assessed.

### SEC-05 — Offer instructions (closing_page) → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
Closing page that carries no fair-housing notice at all. Under §4 a closing page omitting the notice is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. No personal-narrative solicitation; no protected-class terms or proxies, so no §1/§2 finding.

### SEC-06 — Systems and utilities (listing_copy) → `none`
Mechanicals/utilities description. No personal-narrative solicitation, no protected-class terms or proxies. Not a closing page.

### SEC-07 — Meet the sellers and next steps (closing_page) → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
- §1: "send us a personal note about yours along with your offer" solicits a buyer personal narrative.
- §2: "young family"/"family" (familial status) and "churchgoing families" (religion proxy via worship).
- §4: closing page carrying no fair-housing notice.
All three rules trip; labels joined in the standard's order.

### SEC-08 — Statement of brokerage practice (disclosure_block) → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`
First sentence is a complete reproduction of the disclosure (names all nine classes) → exempt from §2; that reproduction contains the only protected-class terms, so no §2 finding (the section's own prose outside the reproduction contains none). Second sentence ("we invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them") solicits a personal narrative → §1. The §3 exemption covers §2 only, so §1 still applies. Not a closing page, so §4 not assessed.

### SEC-09 — About your agent (agent_bio) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`
"Dana reminds every client that the law forbids choosing a buyer on the basis of race, religion, familial status or national origin." This is the agent's own prose naming protected classes (an abridged list — four of nine), so §3 gives no exemption (only a complete reproduction is exempt, and own-prose terms are never covered anyway). No personal-narrative solicitation; not a closing page.

### SEC-10 — Closing checklist (closing_page) → `none`
Closing checklist followed by a reproduction of the disclosure naming all nine classes. Checklist text contains no protected-class terms, so all protected-class terms sit inside a complete reproduction → §3 exempts §2. As a closing page it carries the notice in full (all nine classes) → §4 satisfied. No personal-narrative solicitation.

### SEC-11 — Back-page notice (closing_page) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
Notice names only four classes ("race, color, religion or national origin") — an abridged version (four of nine), so no §3 exemption → §2 applies for the protected-class terms. As a closing page it carries an abridged notice (only some classes) → §4 `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. No personal-narrative solicitation.

## Sign-off posture
- Two closing pages fail §4: **SEC-05** (no notice) and **SEC-11** (abridged, four of nine classes). **SEC-07** also fails §4 with no notice. Only **SEC-10** carries a full notice. These three closing-page failures must be corrected before print.

`disclosure_block`, not a `closing_page`, so §4 is not assessed.

### SEC-05 — Offer instructions (closing_page) → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
Closing page that carries no fair-housing notice at all. Under §4 a closing page omitting
the notice is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. No personal-narrative solicitation; no protected-class
terms or proxies, so no §1/§2 finding.

### SEC-06 — Systems and utilities (listing_copy) → `none`
Mechanicals and utilities description. No personal-narrative solicitation; no
protected-class terms or proxies. Not a closing page.

### SEC-07 — Meet the sellers and next steps (closing_page) → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
- **§1:** "send us a personal note about yours along with your offer" solicits a buyer
  personal narrative.
- **§2:** "young family"/"family" (familial status) and "churchgoing families" (religion
  proxy via worship).
- **§4:** closing page carrying no fair-housing notice.
All three rules trip; labels joined in the standard's order.

### SEC-08 — Statement of brokerage practice (disclosure_block) → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`
The first sentence is a complete reproduction of the disclosure (names all nine classes) →
exempt from §2; that reproduction holds the only protected-class terms, and the section's
own prose outside it contains none, so there is no §2 finding. The second sentence ("we
invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits
them") solicits a personal narrative → §1. The §3 exemption covers §2 only, so §1 still
applies. Not a closing page, so §4 is not assessed.

### SEC-09 — About your agent (agent_bio) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`
"Dana reminds every client that the law forbids choosing a buyer on the basis of race,
religion, familial status or national origin." This is the agent's own prose naming
protected classes, and it is an abridged list (four of nine), so §3 gives no exemption
(only a complete reproduction is exempt, and own-prose terms are never covered anyway). No
personal-narrative solicitation; not a closing page.

### SEC-10 — Closing checklist (closing_page) → `none`
Closing checklist followed by a reproduction of the disclosure naming all nine classes.
The checklist text contains no protected-class terms, so all protected-class terms sit
inside a complete reproduction → §3 exempts §2. As a closing page it carries the notice in
full (all nine classes) → §4 satisfied. No personal-narrative solicitation.

### SEC-11 — Back-page notice (closing_page) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
The notice names only four classes ("race, color, religion or national origin") — an
abridged version (four of nine), so §3 gives no exemption → §2 applies for the
protected-class terms. As a closing page it carries an abridged notice (only some classes)
→ §4 `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. No personal-narrative solicitation.
